question.text: What restrictions apply to insurance companies participating in interest rate derivatives under IRDAI guidelines?

answer.text: Insurance companies are allowed to participate in Interest Rate Futures only, and only for long hedge / hedging forecasted transactions
Insurance companies are prohibited from all interest rate derivatives participation
Insurance companies can trade any interest rate derivatives without restrictions
Insurance companies can only trade through Primary Dealers

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (pp.285-286), IRDAI guidelines allow insurance companies to participate in Interest Rate Futures only, and solely for long hedge or hedging forecasted transactions. They cannot take speculative positions or use other interest rate derivative products. The Trap: Insurance companies are not entirely prohibited — IRF hedging is allowed. They are not without restrictions — both the product (IRF only) and the purpose (long hedge / hedging forecasted transactions) are constrained. The Primary-Dealer-only routing is not in the guidelines. Note: Page 295 repeats the IRF-only long-hedge fact in a sample question — keep the answer narrowly scoped to IRF and long hedging.
